absent: Values of MAX_DATA, MAX_INSNS, MAX_TESTRUNS, MAX_SUBTESTS, MAX_STAGGERED_JMP_SIZE, NR_STAGGERED_JMP_RUNS and SKB test constants.
Full layout and flag encoding of the filter test descriptor beyond fields observed in use.
Behavior of the fill helpers that populate long-jump and staggered-jump instruction streams.
Semantics of program creation, runtime selection, verification, and JIT execution paths.
Segmentation, GSO feature, and packet helper semantics exercised by the fixtures.
Locking beyond migration disable and enable around timed runs.

findings.text: The catalog holds ordered self-test descriptors for control flow. Long-jump entries distinguish runtime taken versus runtime not taken and JIT-known always taken versus never taken outcomes, each marked internal without packet data and completed by a fill helper plus a single expected outcome pair.

Staggered-jump entries form a matrix over unconditional and conditional mnemonics covering equality, inequality, bit test, unsigned ordered and signed ordered comparisons, each replicated for wide immediate, wide register, narrow immediate and narrow register encodings, with a shared repeated-run count and an expected outcome derived from a maximum staggered size.

Packet-backed inputs are built from a static dummy device and caller buffer; the builder rejects oversize requests, allocates maximum-size storage, copies the requested prefix, initializes link and protocol metadata and queue, mark, hash, vlan and device attributes, then positions the network header. Generation returns no data for no-data tests, heap memory for large-memory tests, otherwise the built packet optionally extended with one paged fragment; release mirrors that dispatch.

Filter extent resolution prefers helper-provided length and pointer when present, else scans a fixed static instruction array backward for the last nonzero entry. Creation branches on classic versus internal type: classic builds through a kernel program creator with explicit expected-failure comparison, internal allocates sized storage, copies instructions, records stack depth and zero-extension intent, then selects a runtime. Destruction dispatches to a matching destroy or free routine.

Timed execution captures monotonic timestamps around a fixed iteration loop over the program runner, then normalizes elapsed time per run. The per-filter runner clamps requested runs to a maximum, iterates subtests until a zero size and zero result terminator after the first entry, generates and releases input per subtest, and counts mismatches between observed and expected results.

Init-time filter suite driver walks the full catalog with cooperative rescheduling and range-based exclusion, invokes each fill helper before creation, frees helper-allocated instruction memory after creation, tracks pass, fail and JIT counts, logs per-test status, and reports failure if any case failed.

Init-time segmentation suite driver walks a small table of builders paired with feature sets, excludes by range, builds one packet per case, segments it under the case features, frees segment lists and input, logs per-case outcome, then summarizes pass and fail counts.
Segment-case descriptor associates a label with a no-argument packet builder callback and a network feature set used as segmentation capabilities.

Tail-call case descriptor associates a label with a fixed-capacity internal instruction buffer, a flag word, an expected result, a stack-depth requirement, and a boolean marking presence of a tail-call construct.
Tail-call test ABI uses marker value 0x7a11ca11, null index 0x7fff, and invalid index 0x7ffe.
Tail-call state flags occupy bit zero for need-state and bit one for result-in-state.

Global selection state consists of a single identifier defaulting to negative one and an inclusive range defaulting from zero to maximum integer; exclusion is true when the candidate lies outside the range. A 64-character static buffer holds a test name scratch area.

Two segmentation fixtures construct linked two-packet chains with distinct layouts: one uses paged fragments with head-fragment marking, IPv4 protocol and segmentation offload state plus timestamp; the other uses linear heap buffers with IPv6 protocol, pulled data offsets, frag-list linkage and reduced segment size. Both adjust aggregate length accounting and unwind partial allocations on failure.
Timed execution holds migration disabled across timestamp capture and the full run loop, releasing it only after the final timestamp, so measured iterations do not migrate.

Allocation-failure paths return null or record errors without leaking the companion object: fixture builders free the already-built packet or page, data-generation failure aborts the subtest loop with an error count, and creation failure skips execution while still releasing helper memory.

Test helper callable accepts a single 64-bit argument, formats a fixed sequence of local integers together with the argument into a 64-byte scratch buffer, and returns the formatted length; a companion macro binds the helper identifier to the maximum function identifier.
Tail-call emission helper materializes a short instruction sequence loading the marker into designated registers with a supplied offset before issuing the tail-call transfer.
